cvEn:
Omri Ariav, son of Bruria and Dov, was born on the second day of Tishrei 5688 (28 September 1927) in Ein Harod. He completed his studies at the joint school of Ein Harod and Tel Yosef and grew up in an atmosphere of labor and creativity on the kibbutz. He excelled in sports and was a member of the Hapoel basketball team, winning medals and trophies in track and field. Upon completing his studies at the age of seventeen, he volunteered for the Jewish Brigade and served in Europe. After his discharge, he returned to the kibbutz and worked in the dairy.

In 1948, during the War of Independence, he enlisted in the Air Force and took part in the first pilot training course held in the country. At the end of the course he was certified as a combat pilot in the IDF. Because of the split in the kibbutz movement, he moved to Kvutzat Kvarim together with Tziona, his partner for life, and their son Yerom was born there. While a member of Kvarim, he worked with the company Chimavir and served as a pilot spraying fields and orchards. Two years later, however, he longed to return to the Air Force, and he went back to regular service.

From childhood he stood out for his independence, his thinking and his manner. He was blessed with a noble spirit and was pleasant in his bearing, and these qualities endeared him to everyone who knew him. He fell while carrying out his duties on the nineteenth of Av 5714 (18 August 1954) and was laid to rest in the cemetery in Ein Harod. The Chief of Staff posthumously promoted him to the rank of Lieutenant from the day of his death. He left behind a wife and a two-month-old infant. In 5715 (1955) Ein Harod published a book in his memory. In Beit She'an, a youth culture center called "Beit Omri" was established in his name. In Kfar Yehoshua, where he fell, a memorial monument was erected in his honor.
